{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABjA8irw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhMXOrM", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 415, "title": "Fix desktop dictation stalling after the first insertion until a keyboard event", "body": "## Problem

The user reports a regression in desktop Focused Application Text Output: the first spoken phrase is inserted, but the next phrase is not inserted until the user presses a physical keyboard key. Dictation should deliver successive text chunks automatically without requiring any keyboard interaction beyond Start/Stop.

Reported on 2026-11-27. The current main revision when investigating is [b12a5b0](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/commit/b12a5b0c8997a6d53f132f63c5a4da0246675f33), following #413 / PR #414 (Floating Display). The exact target application, local build revision, and whether the second recognition result had already become final were not specified. Treat macOS desktop as the primary affected host, based on the preceding discussion; do not invent additional reproduction facts.

### Reported reproduction

1. Start desktop dictation with the usual ASR final → Focused Application Text Output connection.
2. Speak a phrase and let it be inserted.
3. Speak another phrase while recording continues, without touching the keyboard.
4. Observed: the subsequent insertion does not appear, but may appear when a physical key is pressed.
5. Expected: each delivered final TEXT is inserted automatically, without any extra keyboard action.

### Investigation leads (not an established root cause)

- [desktop/mac-target.m:151–153](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/b12a5b0c8997a6d53f132f63c5a4da0246675f33/desktop/mac-target.m#L151-L153) uses `held || (GetCurrentKeyModifiers() & ...)` to block Paste while modifiers appear held.
- [Paste dispatch and waiting](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/b12a5b0c8997a6d53f132f63c5a4da0246675f33/desktop/mac-target.m#L264-L312) posts a synthetic Command+V key pair with Command flags and waits again before subsequent chunks. If the synthetic events leave a stale modifier state, the next request could remain waiting until a physical event updates that state. Periodic waiting notifications refresh the host timeout, so an indefinite wait may not surface as an error. This is a plausible explanation, not a reproduced finding.
- Existing [macOS dispatch fixture](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/b12a5b0c8997a6d53f132f63c5a4da0246675f33/tests/desktop/macos-dispatch-fixture.m#L219-L220) mocks both modifier state and CGEvent posting, so it does not by itself establish the behavior of actual synthetic events on macOS.
- PR #414 did not change the native paste helper or ASR implementation, but added floating indicator updates/resizing. Check the relevant final TEXT delivery, queue completion, modifier/event state and indicator/focus interaction as necessary to distinguish a recognition delay from an insertion stall. Do not assume Floating Display is the cause just because the report followed its merge.

## Expected outcome

- Fix the reported ordinary-use failure: multiple successive TEXT chunks are inserted promptly and in order within the same recording, with no intervening physical key press or mouse interaction required. The output queue must advance automatically.
- Identify the actual cause as far as the available environment permits and make the smallest coherent fix. If modifier waiting is responsible, simplify or correct the waiting/dispatch logic so the app's own synthetic Paste cannot block subsequent Paste operations. Check actual physical modifier state separately from synthetic event state where appropriate. Do not add elaborate waiting/recovery frameworks or new user settings. Do not require the user to press another key, switch focus, or restart recording as a workaround.
- Preserve the existing clipboard + native Paste method, ordinary current-focus delivery (#407, #409), generic TEXT sink semantics (#411), and Floating Display (#413). The sink must still honor graph wiring, not filter by ASR stage or producer identity. Keep normal clipboard restoration/ownership guards, explicit Cancel/Stop/Quit and normal OS permission/secure-input handling. Do not restore session-long focus locking or introduce new target restrictions.
- Maintain basic behavior when the actual Start/Stop shortcut modifiers are held, but do not pursue every exceptional key-event timing or third-party application race. No unrelated Linux/extension refactoring, full OS compatibility investigation, or new model work is required.

### Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Add a focused regression test exercising successive nonempty TEXT deliveries in a running session, with no simulated physical key press between them. Verify the second and later Paste operations dispatch automatically, and the queue does not remain waiting. The test should capture the identified failure mechanism rather than merely repeat existing mocks that cannot detect it. Include the relevant regression for genuine shortcut release and/or Floating Display if implicated.
- [ ] Build and launch the macOS package; run `npm test`, applicable focused desktop regression tests, and `git diff --check`. Use the lightest meaningful test layer, including real native events if available under existing permissions. If the runner lacks OS authorization for independent-app input, report that limitation, validate the fix with controlled regression evidence, and supply brief optional manual reproduction/verification steps in the PR. No user action, human approval, new authorized runner, or real-model download is a merge/closure gate.
- [ ] Report the root cause or remaining diagnostic uncertainty accurately, the fix, and actual test outcomes in the PR. Do not claim the exact user environment was verified if it was not. Once the ordinary-use regression is addressed and applicable mandatory checks pass, complete normal review and merge. Do not hold this fix for unrelated or speculative edge-case hardening.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Optional user verification is not a closure condition. A subsequently observed defect can be tracked separately.

## Context

Related #401, #407, #409, #411 and #413 / PR #414. Follow the repository's [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md), and no-human-gate policy.
